meta.description: Exactly right — the common misquote is “We’re.” Roy Scheider ad-libbed the line in Jaws (1975); the credited screenwriters did not write it.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'You're gonna need a bigger boat'?
meta.ogDescription: Wikiquote and AFI both transcribe it as “You’re gonna need a bigger boat.” Roy Scheider improvised it on set — it was never a scripted line.

answer.label: Ad-libbed by
answer.authorDates: 1932–2008 · American actor · Chief Martin Brody in Jaws (1975)
answer.sourceLine: The popular wording is the real wording: Wikiquote’s transcription of Jaws (1975) and the American Film Institute’s official quotes list both give it as “You’re gonna need a bigger boat.” What is not straightforward is where it came from — the screenplay is credited to Peter Benchley and Carl Gottlieb, but the line was never scripted. Scheider ad-libbed it into the scene, and Gottlieb himself says it was already a standing joke among the crew about the boats the production had been given.

source.heading: The line, as transcribed

Peter Benchley and Carl Gottlieb, from Benchley’s 1974 novel — but this line is reported as Scheider’s on-set ad-lib

source.excerpt: “Slow ahead.” I can go slow ahead. Come on down here and chum some of this… [the shark suddenly appears, causing Brody to recoil in shock] You’re gonna need a bigger boat.
trail: The transcription. Wikiquote’s Jaws (film) page lists the line under “Police Chief Martin Brody,” in context and in bold, as “You’re gonna need a bigger boat.” — second person, no ambiguity Wikiquote ↗.

The institutional record agrees. The American Film Institute’s own list prints entry 35 as “You’re gonna need a bigger boat.” — Jaws (1975), writers Peter Benchley and Carl Gottlieb AFI’s 100 Years…100 Movie Quotes ↗.

But the writers did not write it. The BBC’s obituary of Roy Scheider states that his famous line when the shark reveals itself “was ad-libbed by the actor,” and gives the same AFI placing BBC News, 11 February 2008 ↗. That is consistent with how the film was made: Wikipedia’s production account describes scenes being written the night before shooting, with many pieces of dialogue originating in the actors’ improvisations Wikipedia ↗.

Ad-libbing it is not the same as inventing it. The best-placed witness on where the sentence came from is Carl Gottlieb, the credited screenwriter who was on the boats for the whole shoot and later wrote the production memoir The Jaws Log. He told The Hollywood Reporter in 2016 that the line was already a crew catchphrase: Richard Zanuck and David Brown were, in Gottlieb’s words, “very stingy producers”, the crew kept telling them they were gonna need a bigger boat, and it got said whenever anything went wrong on the water — a late lunch, swells rocking the camera ACMI, quoting Gottlieb ↗. Scheider picked the saying up and kept slipping it into takes until one reading landed in the finished film Mental Floss ↗.

No specialist ruling to defer to. A search of Quote Investigator for “bigger boat” returns “Nothing Found” QI search ↗ — QI has not investigated this line, so no specialist finding is being set aside. The wording rests on the film transcription and the AFI list; the origin rests on the credited screenwriter’s own account.
source.excerptNote: As transcribed at Wikiquote, which bolds the final sentence and notes its No. 35 AFI ranking; the bracketed stage direction is Wikiquote’s. One word of Brody’s complaint is elided here.
source.rightsNote: Jaws was released by Universal Pictures on 20 June 1975 and remains in copyright — US public-domain status reaches only works first published through 1930. Screen writing is work-for-hire, so the rights in the film and its dialogue sit with the studio rather than with any individual writer or performer, whatever the origin of a given line.

author.name: Roy Scheider
author.heading: Who put it in the film
author.metaLine: 1932–2008 · American actor · Chief Brody in Jaws (1975)
author.bio: Roy Richard Scheider (10 November 1932 – 10 February 2008) was an American actor whose best-known work came in the 1970s and early 1980s, including The French Connection, Marathon Man and All That Jazz, for which he was Oscar-nominated. His defining role was Amity Island police chief Martin Brody in Steven Spielberg’s Jaws (1975). He appears here as the man who put the film’s most quoted sentence on screen: the BBC’s obituary reports that it was ad-libbed by the actor rather than scripted. He did not coin it, though — by Carl Gottlieb’s account it was a standing joke among the crew about the undersized boats the production had been given, which Scheider carried into a take and made permanent.

misattribution.heading: What actually goes wrong with this one
misattribution.intro: Nothing here is fabricated and nobody is falsely credited with a film they had no part in. The film is real, the line is real, and — unusually — the wording people search for is the wording that was spoken. Two things still go wrong with it, and one of them is the opposite of the usual complaint.

items.why: The pronoun is what people get wrong, and they get it wrong in the direction nobody expects: the corrupted form is “We’re,” not “You’re.” A full-text search across the Internet Archive’s scanned books shows the “We’re” version in print again and again — trivia collections, business books, comics, craft manuals — and turns up “They’re gonna need a bigger boat” and “I think we’re gonna need a bigger boat” for good measure see the results ↗. The line as transcribed is second person: Brody is telling Quint, whose boat it is.

items.tag: credited — but not for this sentence
items.why: They are the credited screenwriters, and AFI prints their names beside the quote at No. 35 on its list AFI’s 100 Movie Quotes ↗, which is why the line is routinely treated as a piece of screenwriting. The BBC’s obituary of Roy Scheider says otherwise: the line “was ad-libbed by the actor” BBC News ↗, and Gottlieb himself places the sentence off-script entirely — a catchphrase the crew were already using before it was ever a line ACMI ↗. Credit for the screenplay and authorship of this particular sentence are not the same claim.

misattribution.truthLine: The sentence in the film is “You’re gonna need a bigger boat” — transcribed that way at Wikiquote ↗ and printed that way in AFI’s official list ↗. It was never in the screenplay: Roy Scheider ad-libbed it into the scene, carrying in a joke the crew had been making at the producers’ expense about the boats they were given Carl Gottlieb’s account ↗.

context.heading: The line the audience drowned out
lead: Brody is shovelling chum off the stern, complaining about it, and not looking at the water when the shark surfaces behind him. The reaction is the joke; the sentence is the punchline. It works because it is the smallest possible response to the largest possible problem — a municipal budgeting observation delivered to a great white shark.

It very nearly did not land. Wikipedia’s production history records that at test screenings the audience’s screams covered the one-liner entirely, so the filmmakers extended Brody’s reaction after the shark appears and raised the volume of the line. The most quoted sentence in the film had to be rescued in the edit — and it was never in the script to begin with.
context.detailsSummary: How a film shot without a finished script produced its own best line
detailsBody: Carl Gottlieb was hired for what was meant to be a one-week dialogue polish and ended up the primary screenwriter, rewriting nearly the whole script across the nine weeks of principal photography. Wikipedia’s account of the production notes that each scene’s pages were typically finished the night before shooting, after Gottlieb had dinner with Spielberg and members of the cast and crew to decide what would go in — and that many pieces of dialogue originated in the actors’ improvisations at those dinners, with a few created on set just before filming.

That is the working method that makes an unscripted line plausible rather than legendary — but it is background, not the explanation for this one. Gottlieb’s own account points somewhere else: not a dinner-table improvisation, but a running gag the unit made at the producers’ expense about the boats they had been given, which Scheider kept feeding into takes until one landed. Either way, the screen credit and the authorship of any single sentence are different questions here: Benchley and Gottlieb hold the credit, John Milius and others contributed uncredited polishes, and the film’s most famous line came from neither the script nor the rewrites.
context.pull: The most quoted line in Jaws started as a complaint about the budget.

sourcesVerified.claim: The film's dialogue, as transcribed, reads "You're gonna need a bigger boat." (second person), spoken by Police Chief Martin Brody after the shark surfaces behind him while he is chumming.

AFI's 100 Years...100 Movie Quotes lists at No. 35 "You're gonna need a bigger boat." from Jaws (1975), with writers given as Peter Benchley and Carl Gottlieb and production company Universal Pictures / Zanuck-Brown.
Scheider's famous line when the shark reveals itself, "You're gonna need a bigger boat", was ad-libbed by the actor; it made number 35 in AFI's list. Scheider was born in Orange, New Jersey, in 1932.

Credited screenwriter Carl Gottlieb, quoted from The Hollywood Reporter (2016), says the line originated on set: "[Richard] Zanuck and [David] Brown were very stingy producers so everyone kept telling them 'You're gonna need a bigger boat'", and it "became a catchphrase for anytime anything went wrong - if lunch was late or the swells were rocking the camera". The page also notes the line's No. 35 AFI ranking. (ACMI prints the producers' first names transposed as "[David] Zanik and [Richard] Brown"; the producers were Richard D. Zanuck and David Brown, and Mental Floss quotes the same Gottlieb line with the names the right way round.)

Reporting the same Gottlieb account: the line "was famously ad-libbed by Scheider, but ... the actor didn't pull the line out of thin air"; crew members complained to producers that the production's support boat was too small, "which is how they coined the soon-to-be-famous phrase"; and "Scheider eventually picked up the saying and started sneaking it into takes."

Jaws is a 1975 American thriller directed by Steven Spielberg, based on the 1974 novel by Peter Benchley; screenplay credited to Benchley and Carl Gottlieb, who rewrote it during principal photography; released 20 June 1975; studios Zanuck/Brown Company and Universal Pictures. Many pieces of dialogue originated from the actors' improvisations, with scripts typically finished the night before shooting. At test screenings the audience's screams covered Scheider's "bigger boat" one-liner, so Brody's reaction was extended and the line's volume raised.
Roy Richard Scheider, November 10, 1932 - February 10, 2008, American actor; his ad-libbed line "You're gonna need a bigger boat" was voted 35th on AFI's list of best movie quotes.
Quote Investigator has no article on this quotation - a site search for "bigger boat" returns "Nothing Found".

Published books repeatedly print the corrupted form "We're gonna need a bigger boat" (and variants such as "They're gonna need a bigger boat" and "I think we're gonna need a bigger boat") when quoting Jaws, alongside the correct "You're" form.
